summary: Michiyo Hoshi is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. Hoshi held posts at Toyo Bunko, attested in 2003, and at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa.

Midori Nishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Nishino pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later held a research post there, attested between 2010 and 2015.

Migmar Tsering (d. 1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Khenpo Appey. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990), headed Sakya College (attested 1991–1997), and was affiliated with the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2006).

Mihai Șora (1916–2023) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest under Mircea Eliade (~1934–1938), the University of Paris (~1939–1945), and the CNRS (~1945–1948). He worked at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1954–1969).

Mikaël Bauer specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard University under Ryuichi Abe, attested in 2010.

Mikel Burley works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Essex (1990–1993), under Jay M. Bernstein, Jonardon Ganeri, and Brian Carr, and completed a PhD at the University of Bristol (2005) under John Peacock. He joined the University of Leeds (attested 2007–2020).
Mikio Otsuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. In 2007, Otsuki was attested as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

Mikisaburo Mori (1909–1986) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Osaka University (PhD 1962). He held posts at Kyoto University, Osaka High School, Osaka University (1950–1973), and Bukkyo University (~1973–1983).

Milman Parry (1902–1935) was a linguist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet (1924–1928). He held a post at Harvard University from circa 1929 to 1935.

Milton Singer (1912–1994) worked in Indology, religious studies, and anthropology. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1930–1936) and the University of Chicago (~1936–1940), where he later served as a faculty member (~1940–1979).
Min Ling Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin was a scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Min Thu Wun (1909–2004) was a scholar in linguistics and literature. He studied at the University of Rangoon under Pe Maung Tin (~1926–1935) and continued his studies at the University of Oxford (~1936–1939).

Ming Mei specializes in Sinology and history and archaeology. Mei earned an MPhil at The University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, and also studied at SOAS University of London and under Andrey Terentyev.

Ming-Wood Liu (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. After studying at The University of Hong Kong (BA 1966–1974) and UCLA (PhD 1974–1979) under Kenneth K. S. Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, he served as a professor at The University of Hong Kong (~1979–2008).
Mingyu Fu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Huifeng Shi, attested in 2013.

Minori Nishimura (b. 1947) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Taisho University (~1970–1976) under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, later serving as an associate professor there (~1993–2017) and as a researcher at the Sanko Cultural Institute (attested 2002).

Minoru Hara (1930–2021) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard University, served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1975–1991), and directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Minoru Kiyota (1923–2013) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at UC Berkeley (~1946–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1952–1963) under Reimon Yuki, Shinsho Hanayama, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa, and served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1963–2013).

Minton Warren (1850–1907) was a linguist who studied at Tufts, Yale under William Dwight Whitney, Leipzig, Bonn, and Strasbourg (Dr. phil.). He served as a Latin professor at Johns Hopkins University (1879–1899) and Harvard University (1899).
Minyak Kunzang Sonam was a scholar who pursued his studies under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
